approved: Strengthening Oversight of the National Intelligence Community Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would add new rules for consulting and notifying others before making regulations that define 'intelligence function' for the Department of Home Affairs.

It would also make minor technical changes to the Intelligence Services Act to clarify the Committee's role, modernise procedures, and improve how the Commonwealth Ombudsman and the Inspector-General jointly oversee Home Affairs.
The Inspector-General would have to tell the Committee if they decide not to investigate a matter the Committee referred to them.
Adds consultation and notification requirements for regulations defining 'intelligence function' for the Department of Home Affairs.
Makes minor technical amendments to the Intelligence Services Act to clarify the Committee's functions and modernise procedural provisions.
Requires the Inspector-General to advise the Committee when they decline to inquire into a referred matter.
The Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security, the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Intelligence and Security, and the Department of Home Affairs.
Moved to suspend standing order 111 paragraphs (5) to (8) so four named bills could be considered during the period of sittings; the question was agreed to.
